Boosie Asked Trump to Pardon His Federal Gun Charge Before He Got Scammed (Flashback)
recentItems.description: In this flashback, Boosie opened up to VladTV about his ongoing efforts to secure a presidential pardon for his federal gun charge from President Donald Trump. Boosie claimed that his case had previously been dismissed before he was recharged under President Biden’s Department of Justice, while also criticizing Biden for pardoning his son, Hunter Biden. Amid his legal battle, Boosie revealed that he unexpectedly received an invitation to the White House for a Black History Month event. Accompanied by his attorney, Boosie was set to attend a dinner honoring prominent Black figures, which he described as a major milestone in his career and life. Boosie also expressed hope that he would have an opportunity to speak with Trump personally and make an appeal for a pardon, though he acknowledged that a resolution was unlikely to come soon, as his case remained pending before the Supreme Court.

recentItems.title: Trap Lore Ross on Attending Entire Lil Durk Trial,3 Bodyguards Protected Him from Durk Fans (Part 2)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 1: https://youtu.be/fgzkOWzO-eY
--------

Trap Lore Ross joins VladTV after sitting through every day of the federal Lil Durk trial, where Durk was found not guilty on five counts while another charge remains pending. Ross describes the tense courthouse scene, explaining why he went from no security to three bodyguards as crowds of Durk supporters surrounded him on federal grounds. He also breaks down what the jury heard, why he respected the verdict, and how defense lawyers Brian Christie and Marissa challenged the government’s case. The conversation also covers co-defendants DD and David Lindsay, who were found guilty on serious counts tied to the death of Lul Pab, plus key evidence involving Quando Rondo, cell site data, alleged stalking, FaceTime calls, cooperating witnesses, and reasonable doubt. A firsthand look at one of hip-hop’s most closely watched legal cases.

In this VladTV conversation, Max B reflects on a pivotal era in New York hip-hop, from selling his publishing for $120,000 to bonding out while a murder case still loomed over his career. He breaks down how he first linked with French Montana during the Cocaine City DVD days, when French was still fighting to be taken seriously as a rapper, and how their chemistry helped fuel a run of mixtapes and viral street coverage.

The interview also revisits the tension surrounding Jim Jones, Cam’ron, Bird Gang, and footage circulating through Cocaine City, WorldStar, and VladTV. Max B addresses the chair-throwing incident tied to a Brooklyn confrontation with Jim Jones’ crew, describing the chaotic atmosphere and the people around him at the time. From Harlem to Brooklyn, this is a candid look at music, beef, media, and survival during a turbulent chapter in Max B’s story.

recentItems.title: Vlad Reacts to Boosie 60 Minutes Interview, Addresses Rumor Boosie Can Be Charged for Bribery
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

In this VladTV breakdown, DJ Vlad reviews Boosie Badazz’s CBS 60 Minutes interview about allegedly paying $600,000 to Republican consultants Jacob Wohl and Jack Burkman in hopes of securing a Donald Trump pardon. Vlad examines the viral claim that Boosie could face bribery charges, citing attorney Bradford Cohen — known for his work on Lil Wayne and Kodak Black’s Trump-era pardons — who says Boosie appears more like an alleged victim than a criminal target. The discussion also covers reported text messages naming figures like Laura Loomer, Erica Kirk, Mike Johnson and Natalie Harp, plus Boosie’s criticism that 60 Minutes left out key context involving Alice Marie Johnson, the White House pardon process, and his ongoing legal dispute. Vlad also reflects on mainstream exposure, civil lawsuit possibilities, and where Boosie stands with VladTV after a year away from the platform.

Chingy joins VladTV to revisit a memorable chapter involving Janet Jackson, Jermaine Dupri, and his second album, *Powerballin’*. After Vlad recalls meeting Janet and Stevie Wonder at Johnny Gill’s New Year’s party, Chingy shares how Janet ended up appearing on his song “Don’t Worry” and how a phone call from the pop icon caught him completely off guard.  

The St. Louis rapper says Janet’s team told him she admired him, then recalls a night out during her relationship with Jermaine Dupri where he felt she kept staring in his direction. Chingy reflects with humor on believing he could have had a chance, while still showing respect for Janet’s iconic status, beauty, and legacy. The conversation also touches on celebrity crushes, money, fame, and the unforgettable early-2000s hip-hop/R&B era.

Shawn Prez sits down with former Army Ranger sniper Nicholas Irving to discuss Donald Trump’s unusual Republican midterm convention, nicknamed “Trumpet Palooza,” at American Airlines Arena in Dallas, Texas. Irving argues the event reflects political pressure as voters face stubborn gas prices, rising grocery bills, higher cost of living, and doubts about campaign promises like “drill, baby, drill.”  

The conversation also examines whether Trump and Republican leaders will address the ongoing military conflict, questions around claims of victory, nuclear weapons concerns, the closed Strait, and the human and financial costs facing American families. Prez challenges the idea that the mission has been accomplished, while Irving frames the convention as more entertainment than policy.  

A sharp political breakdown on midterms, Trump rallies, the economy, war messaging, and what voters may actually be looking for in 2024.
